name: – Marcos Ros Sempere – § 10 – Am 4
title: REPORT on a new strategy for media literacy and digital learning
part_text: 10. Highlights that any cooperation between public and private stakeholders, or civil society organisations involved in media literacy must comply with the highest standards of financial transparency and political neutrality and must not promote, support or engage in political campaigning; considers that where a systemic risk of conflicts of interest is identified, funding should be suspended and reviewed, applying the same standards and criteria to all organisations without discrimination; recalls that media literacy education can only take place within the framework of freedom of expression protected from all political control and the risk that media literacy programmes financed by the Commission, under the guise of combating disinformation, could be used to harmonise media content and discredit sources of information that are critical of the EU; calls on the Member States, consequently, to retain full control over the design and implementation of media literacy education, while fully respecting pluralism of opinion and freedom of expression;
